topline.text: Sheffield's Talbot Specialist School - a council-run SEND school - saw NEU members walk out on 5 November, with further strike days threatened across the month in a dispute over workload and safe working practices.
topline.action: Worth noting if AP/SEND placement conversations touch Talbot's capacity over the coming weeks.

topline.text: Otherwise another quiet 24-48 hours nationally - no new DfE, Ofsted, safeguarding or funding story cleared the corroboration bar, so today's edition stays short rather than padded.
Reminder: DfE's call for evidence on exclusion reform closes in 10 days, on 19 November.

diary.text: DfE's call for evidence on school exclusion reform (behaviour strategies, in-school units, managed moves) closes - 10 days away.
DfE due to publish autumn 2025/26 suspensions and permanent exclusions statistics for England.

items.lede: NEU strike action hits Talbot Specialist School.
items.body: Staff at Talbot Specialist School - one of the few Sheffield schools still maintained directly by the council rather than a trust - walked out on Thursday 5 November, with the NEU threatening several more strike days across November. The union cites excessive workload and unsafe working practices; the council has asked members to reconsider.
items.action: Flag to the inclusion team if ongoing disruption affects SEND placement or referral capacity at Talbot over the coming weeks.

items.body: DfE's call for evidence on exclusion reform - covering behaviour strategies, in-school units and managed moves - closes in 10 days, on 19 November. The accompanying autumn 2025/26 suspensions and permanent exclusions statistics are still due this month, with no exact publication date confirmed yet.
items.action: Last call for the inclusion team to get any evidence in before the window closes.

box.quote: Failing to engage in meaningful dialogue.
box.author: Rafia Hussain, NEU Sheffield branch secretary, on the Talbot dispute
